Subject: Production impact: throughput drop & 5xx after v5.1 q-profile switch

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sudden throughput collapse and a ~3% 5xx spike on our production API around 08:30 PT after Redwood pushed the v5.1 q-profile change this morning. Latency p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~720ms for our high-concurrency endpoints and overall TPS dropped ~40%. This is affecting our checkout flow — we're throttling traffic manually now.

We've attached a short snippet of the support logs and a few traces. Can you please confirm whether the q-profile change was applied to our dedicated pool? We need immediate mitigation and a rollback if possible.

Sample contacts: ops+eng@auroraedge.com (on-call).

Thanks — this is urgent.

Megan Li

Forwarded message follows — internal triage notes below.

--- Forwarded original email from Megan Li retained above ---

Internal triage summary (quick):
- Rishi: early signal looks like q-profile v5.1 increases kernel invocations for short sequences which is amplifying scheduling overhead under high concurrency. Combined with a small change in KV-cache handling in v5.1, we've got backpressure on the hotpath.
- Observed: greater variance in per-request GPU occupancy + increased selector latency in the serving runtime.

Proposed immediate mitigation plan (30–90m):
1) Toggle AuroraEdge's routing policy to the previous safe variant (v5.0-q-safe) — this is non-disruptive and we've used it for quick fallbacks.
2) Temporarily raise reserved capacity by +1 GPU equivalent for 45 minutes to absorb backpressure while we observe.
3) Run quick hotpath profiling (Rishi) and produce a 1-page hotpath-analysis we can share externally.

I'll prepare the rollback instructions and a short exec note for Vanessa. If Kimberley and Rishi agree, I'll post the rollback doc to the thread and request sign-off from Megan for the 15:00 PT window (we want a predictable low-traffic window but will do ASAP if they prefer).

Attachments: hotpath-analysis.pdf (draft — internal)
Jira: RED-1342 (created)

Subject: Re: Production impact: throughput drop & 5xx after v5.1 q-profile switch

Megan — quick update and proposed remediation: 

What we saw: early telemetry indicates the v5.1 q-profile increased selector/kernel swaps for short sequences on your hot endpoints which, under peak concurrency, created transient queueing and a higher error surface. Rishi's hotpath draft is attached.

Immediate action we propose (minimizes customer impact):
1) Roll back AuroraEdge routing to v5.0-q-safe now. This is a variant toggle (no model weight fetch required) and typically takes <90s to fully route.
2) Provision +1 reserved GPU equivalent to the Dedicated pool for the next 60 minutes to absorb in-flight requests while routing finishes.
3) Post-rollback: we will run a short canary and share p95/p99 and 5xx deltas. If stable, we'll schedule a controlled re-roll of v5.1 after we patch the q-profile's short-sequence path.

Requested from you: two request IDs from ~08:30 window (if available) — those will speed correlation. Also confirm whether you prefer us to execute rollback immediately or wait for a 15:00 PT maintenance window. We recommend immediate toggle to limit customer-visible errors.

Attachments: rollback_instructions.pdf (step-by-step for toggle + capacity bump)

Thanks,
Kimberly

Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: throughput drop & 5xx after v5.1 q-profile switch — rollback complete

Status update for leadership and post-mortem prep:

Timeline:
- 11:15 PT: toggled AuroraEdge routing to v5.0-q-safe and applied +1 reserved GPU equivalent.
- 11:18 PT: p95 reduced from ~720ms to ~230ms, throughput recovered to within 98% of baseline, 5xx rate returned to baseline.
- 11:55 PT: capacity bump removed; steady state confirmed during a 30-minute observation window.

Root cause (short): a q-profile optimizer introduced an extra kernel selection path for short sequences which increased per-request scheduling jitter under high concurrency. That path didn't fail safety checks for latency regressions in our earlier synthetic tests because our test workload didn't exercise the same short-sequence distribution.

Next steps (owned):
- Rishi: patch q-profile to remove the high-overhead path and add a dedicated short-sequence microbenchmark to the release gate. (RED-1342)
- Marissa: prepare an external RCA and timing for a controlled re-roll.
- Vanessa: prepare executive summary for AuroraEdge C-suite.

I'll attach the quick metrics snapshot to RED-1342 and link the Drive folder with the hotpath graphs. Early trust signal is good — customer confirmed checkout flows recovered.

-Rishi Malhotra
